set.name: Shirorekha
set.mechanism: The Devanagari headline that joins letters into one word: a gold line holds three grains in the mark, gives the inscriptional capitals their hanging rule, and is the only gold in a forest-and-ivory palette.
set.expression_move: The gold joining line: the single bright element in mark, layout and pack.
set.differs_by: Category marks are crests, monuments and leaves on maroon or kraft; this is a script-derived abstract mark in deep forest with one line of gold, no illustration.

logo.concept: One line joins three grains into a single word: shirorekha, panicle and toran at once.

misuse.label: Do not join the grains to the line
Never add or remove grains: always three

defaults_used.why: The brief asks for warm ivory, and ivory is the live Sangat site's ground (equity).
The brief asks for a muted gold accent; it is held to one element (line, dot, grain or seal), never a frame or foil flood.

rationale.claim: The Devanagari headline that joins letters into one word: a gold line holds three grains in the mark, gives the inscriptional capitals their hanging rule, and is the only gold in a forest-and-ivory palette.

Category shelf (judgement, sites unreachable here): maroon/red + gold foil with monuments and crowns (India Gate, Daawat, Kohinoor, Lal Qilla), purple/navy script (Tilda), leaf-green kraft and badges (24 Mantra, Organic Tattva).
All faces are OFL Google Fonts designed with both Latin and Devanagari, so Hindi lines use the brand's own type rather than a fallback.

set.name: Bindu
set.mechanism: One golden point: the dot that romanises संगत as SAṄGAT sits over the N, and the same single point is the only colour in an ink-on-paper palette and the only mark the pack needs.
set.expression_move: The golden bindu over the N; everything else is black-green ink on paper.
set.differs_by: Against ornate, illustrated packs this is a pure typographic identity with one dot: the quietest pack on a loud shelf.

set.name: Mohar
set.mechanism: A trader's seal: संगत cut through a gold stamp is the mark, the high-contrast Indian display face is the seal's voice, and a night-forest ground lets the gold stamp carry the pack.
set.expression_move: The gold Devanagari seal on a dark ground.
set.differs_by: Heritage without monuments: a living craft instead of a palace, and dark forest instead of maroon; the only dark-ground premium pack on a light or red shelf.

logo.concept: The name in Devanagari, cut through a gold seal: Sangat stamped as a promise.

defaults_used.why: The brief asks for a muted gold accent; here it is the seal itself, a single object.
The square is the seal block (a mohar is a stamp); the full Devanagari name is cut through it, not an initial in an app tile.

set.name: Saath
set.mechanism: Moving forward together: two grains lean forward side by side in the mark, the condensed contemporary sans leans on its verticals, and a cool monsoon green carries one golden grain a step ahead.
set.expression_move: The golden grain a step ahead: motion in an otherwise upright system.
set.differs_by: The category is static and ceremonial; this is the only contemporary, forward-moving mark and the only condensed sans on the shelf.

logo.concept: Two basmati grains stride side by side; the golden one is a step ahead.
